reason: E1 shows RTA increases coercivity in FeCoNiMnCu films via strain-induced anisotropy and domain wall pinning, supporting the mechanism. E2 shows defects from HPT act as pinning centers, increasing coercivity, which supports the general pinning premise. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence for interstitial nitrogen in FeCoNi or its effect on strain and coercivity; the specific claim about nitrogen-induced strain and controlled uptake is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Rapid thermal annealing (RTA) can increase coercivity in fcc high-entropy alloy films via microstructural changes and strain-induced anisotropy enhancement.
Strain-induced anisotropy enhances domain wall pinning, increasing coercivity.
Interstitial nitrogen incorporation into an fcc lattice can create local lattice distortions and nanoscale strain fields.
Domain wall pinning by defects or strain fields increases coercivity without significantly lowering saturation magnetization.
Controlled nitrogen uptake without nitride formation is achievable by tuning annealing atmosphere and temperature.
